original_question: Do the compact Lie groups SU(3), Sp(2) (equivalently Spin(5)), Sp(3), or G2 contain pairs of finite subgroups that are almost conjugate but not conjugate?
target_in_paper: Question 7.5 in §7 (Isospectrality between quotients of symmetric spaces). ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31p.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official wording: it names exactly the four ambient groups appearing in Question 7.5 and asks about the existence of almost conjugate but non-conjugate subgroups; it also correctly records the identification Sp(2) ≃ Spin(5). ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31p.pdf))
missing_details: The paper asks this separately for each ambient group K ∈ {SU(3), Sp(2) ≃ Spin(5), Sp(3), G2}; the draft can be read ambiguously as asking whether at least one of these groups has such a pair, rather than posing four parallel existence questions. ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31p.pdf))

To make the question stand-alone, “almost conjugate” should be defined: there must exist a bijection φ: Γ1 → Γ2 such that each γ ∈ Γ1 is conjugate in K to φ(γ). ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31p.pdf))

To make “not conjugate” explicit, one should say that there is no g ∈ K with gΓ1g^{-1} = Γ2. This is the ambient-group notion relevant throughout the paper. ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31p.pdf))

In the surrounding §7 context, the relevant objects are finite subgroups Γ1, Γ2 ≤ K, because Proposition 7.4 uses such pairs to produce isospectral non-isometric quotients K/Γi endowed with the metric induced by a bi-invariant metric on K. ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31p.pdf))
refined_question: For each compact simple Lie group K ∈ {SU(3), Sp(2) ≃ Spin(5), Sp(3), G2}, does there exist a pair of finite subgroups Γ1, Γ2 ≤ K such that Γ1 and Γ2 are almost conjugate in K—that is, there exists a bijection φ: Γ1 → Γ2 with γ conjugate to φ(γ) in K for every γ ∈ Γ1—but Γ1 and Γ2 are not conjugate as subgroups of K? ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31p.pdf))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation to your draft: the paper states this as Question 7.5 in §7. The nearby context that makes the question precise is Definition 2.1, which defines “almost conjugate,” and Proposition 7.4, which explains why finite almost-conjugate/non-conjugate subgroups of a compact simple Lie group matter for the isospectral-quotient problem. The broader surrounding motivation is Question 1.15 and Theorem 1.16, but those are about which compact simply connected irreducible symmetric spaces cover isospectral non-isometric manifolds; they are broader than, and not explicitly proved equivalent to, Question 7.5. So the refined question should stay at the narrow group-theoretic existence level rather than broaden to a statement about isospectral manifolds or all compact symmetric spaces. ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31p.pdf))
